evidenceBase: https://github.com/sriram-um/aws-serverless-application (main @ a25f479) + read-only checks of account 977534234172 on 2026-10-24

priorities.title: How do you determine what your priorities are?
priorities.notes:
Evidence: requirements come from the exercise sheet, turned into a phased plan (README Progress); trade-offs are written down per decision (README 'Design decisions': caching as a cost toggle, direct integration vs Lambda, single-node DAX, global table migration).
Gap: no threat model, no written governance/compliance requirements (none apply to a portfolio project, but that was never evaluated explicitly).

ops-model.title: How do you structure your organization to support your business outcomes?
ops-model.notes:
Single-maintainer portfolio project: the repository owner owns all resources, scripts and operations; every resource is tagged project=serverless-orders. Changes are requested and reviewed through GitHub pull requests (CI runs tests on PRs).
Gap: no formal mechanism for ownership/responsibilities - not needed for one person, required for a team.

not_applicable_choices.ops_ops_model_def_neg_team_agreements: Single maintainer - no teams to agree responsibilities between.

org-culture.title: How does your organizational culture support your business outcomes?
org-culture.notes: Single-person portfolio project: there is no organization, team or executive sponsor to evaluate.

observability.title: How do you implement observability in your workload?
observability.notes:
Evidence: structured JSON logs (Powertools Logger) with correlation id and git SHA; API Gateway, Lambda, WAF, SQS metrics; X-Ray active tracing with DynamoDB calls as subsegments (template.yaml L40-41, L307).
Gap: no KPIs/SLOs defined (e.g. p99 latency, order success rate); no user-experience telemetry (no CloudWatch Synthetics canary / RUM); API Gateway access logs are not enabled.

dev-integ.title: How do you reduce defects, ease remediation, and improve flow into production?
dev-integ.notes:
Evidence: Git + GitHub; 25 pytest/moto unit tests on every push and PR; sam validate --lint (cfn-lint) before deploy; SAM parameters + samconfig config envs; GitHub Actions builds and deploys on push to main (.github/workflows/deploy.yml); shared standards in PORTFOLIO-PLAYBOOK.md; one small commit per exercise.
Gap: single environment (no dev/staging); no automated patch management (pinned Powertools layer and DAX client are bumped by hand, no Dependabot).

mit-deploy-risks.title: How do you mitigate deployment risks?
mit-deploy-risks.notes:
Evidence: CloudFormation change sets roll back automatically on failure; the whole stack can be recreated from code (scripts/rebuild.sh, proven 4m38s from nothing); CI smoke test after deploy (unauthenticated POST must return 401).
Gap: deployments are not tested in a pre-production environment; no safe deployment strategy (no Lambda aliases with CodeDeploy canary/linear via DeploymentPreference); a failing smoke test does not roll back automatically; the smoke test only checks the auth path.

ready-to-support.title: How do you know that you are ready to support a workload?
ready-to-support.notes:
Evidence: the builder operates the system; runbooks as scripts and docs: scripts/rebuild.sh, scripts/teardown.sh, scripts/smoke_test.sh, README 'Teardown and rebuild' and the DR runbook table (exercise 11).
Gap: no operational readiness review before go-live; no playbooks for investigating issues (e.g. 5XX spike, DLQ messages); no AWS Support plan beyond Basic.

workload-observability.title: How do you utilize workload observability in your organization?
workload-observability.notes:
Evidence: CloudWatch dashboard as code (template.yaml L818-916); latency, cold start and trace analyses recorded in the README (Logs Insights on REPORT lines and the aws/spans log group).
Gap: NO actionable alerts - there is not a single AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm in the template, so errors, throttles, 5XX, DLQ depth and stream IteratorAge are only visible if someone opens the dashboard.

operations-health.title: How do you understand the health of your operations?
operations-health.notes: Gap: no operations goals/KPIs (deploy frequency, change failure rate, time to restore) are measured, communicated or reviewed.

event-response.title: How do you manage workload and operations events?
event-response.notes:
Evidence: status is visible on the CloudWatch dashboard.
Gap: no event/incident/problem process, no process per alert (there are no alerts), no prioritisation or escalation paths, no customer communication plan, no automated responses (e.g. EventBridge rule on DLQ messages).

evolve-ops.title: How do you evolve operations?
evolve-ops.notes:
Evidence: per-phase loop with a README update after every exercise; root causes of real problems documented with fixes (KMS first-use failure, OIDC sub mismatch, StartingPosition LATEST skipping orders, the API being briefly public); lessons fed into the shared PORTFOLIO-PLAYBOOK.md gotchas table; changes validated with before/after measurements (Power Tuning, cold start).
Gap: no regular operations-metrics review, no defined drivers or allocated time for improvement.

performing-architecture.title: How do you select the appropriate cloud resources and architecture patterns for your workload?
performing-architecture.notes: Evidence: serverless managed services throughout; decisions and trade-offs in README 'Design decisions'; cost in docs/cost-estimate.md (caching scenario A vs B); the playbook makes this project the reference architecture for later ones; benchmarks drive choices: direct integration vs Lambda latency, DAX vs DynamoDB reads, replication lag (median 539 ms), Power Tuning for memory.

compute-hardware.title: How do you select and use compute resources in your workload?
compute-hardware.notes:
Evidence: AWS Lambda on arm64 (Graviton) for all functions (template.yaml L33-38); Duration/Invocations/Errors/Throttles on the dashboard; Lambda scales automatically; memory right-sized with Power Tuning: 512 MB for CreateOrder/GetOrder, 256 MB default (template.yaml L104-106); init cost measured inside Lambda.
N/A: hardware accelerators are not relevant.

data-management.title: How do you store, manage, and access data in your workload?
data-management.notes:
Evidence: DynamoDB key-value model (orderId/itemId) for orders and a separate aggregates table for analytics, so reads are key lookups, never scans (template.yaml L59-92, L585-608); on-demand capacity, streams, TTL, global table evaluated and used; DAX and replication latency measured and recorded in the README; DAX read-through cache and API Gateway cache behind EnableCaching.
Gap: DynamoDB metrics (latency, throttles) are not on the dashboard.

networking.title: How do you select and configure networking resources in your workload?
networking.notes:
Evidence: regional API endpoint chosen deliberately (WAF and cache attach to the stage; CDN possible later); for DAX, a free gateway endpoint for DynamoDB and an interface endpoint for X-Ray instead of a NAT gateway; network impact measured (API Gateway service call ~28 ms vs ~7 ms SDK call; cross-region replication ~0.5 s).
N/A: no dedicated connectivity/VPN, load balancers or custom protocols in a serverless API. Gap: region chosen by default (us-east-1), not by user location; no metric-driven network tuning.

not_applicable_choices.perf_networking_choose_appropriate_dedic: No on-premises network or VPN - public serverless API only.
not_applicable_choices.perf_networking_load_balancing_distribut: No load balancers - API Gateway and Lambda distribute traffic as managed services.

process-culture.title: What process do you use to support more performance efficiency for your workload?
process-culture.notes:
Evidence: CloudWatch dashboard and X-Ray; a written optimisation method (playbook 'Lambda optimization method': package size -> Power Tuning -> cold start -> init breakdown -> data-backed change only).
Gap: no performance KPIs, no regular metric reviews, no load test (Power Tuning ran 50 invocations, not a load test), no automated remediation, runtime/layer updates are manual.

manage-service-limits.title: How do you manage service quotas and constraints?
manage-service-limits.notes:
Evidence: fixed limits handled in the design - max 25 lines per order (BatchWriteItem limit) enforced in validation (src/create_order/app.py L39-40); one event source mapping per function+stream (documented 409 pitfall); DAX cluster name <= 20 chars; stage throttle well below the account's API Gateway limit.
Gap: quotas are not monitored (Service Quotas / Trusted Advisor alarms), not managed across accounts/regions, and no headroom was checked for a failover to us-west-2.

planning-network-topology.title: How do you plan your network topology?
planning-network-topology.notes:
Evidence: public entry point is API Gateway (regional, managed across AZs); the optional DAX VPC uses 10.20.0.0/16 with two /24 private subnets in two AZs, leaving room to grow (template.yaml L407-440).
N/A: no on-premises connectivity, no multiple VPCs to connect (hub-and-spoke and non-overlapping ranges don't apply).

not_applicable_choices.rel_planning_network_topology_ha_conn_pr: No on-premises environment or private network connectivity.
not_applicable_choices.rel_planning_network_topology_prefer_hub: At most one VPC (optional DAX) - nothing to interconnect.
not_applicable_choices.rel_planning_network_topology_non_overla: At most one VPC, not connected to any other network.

service-architecture.title: How do you design your workload service architecture?
service-architecture.notes: Evidence: small single-purpose functions (CreateOrder, GetOrder, AnalyticsAggregator, AnalyticsApi) split by domain (orders vs analytics); the API contract is an OpenAPI 3.0.1 definition in the template with every route, parameter and response declared (template.yaml L143-304).

prevent-interaction-failure.title: How do you design interactions in a distributed system to prevent failures?
prevent-interaction-failure.notes:
Evidence: synchronous request/response API and an asynchronous stream pipeline, both documented; analytics are loosely coupled to order creation through DynamoDB Streams (an aggregator failure never fails an order).
Gap: POST /orders is not idempotent - a client retry after a timeout creates a duplicate order (no Idempotency-Key header / Powertools idempotency utility). The stream consumer IS idempotent (eventID marker).
Gap: no constant-work design.

mitigate-interaction-failure.title: How do you design interactions in a distributed system to mitigate or withstand failures?
mitigate-interaction-failure.notes:
Evidence: stage throttling + WAF rate limit; stream retries capped at 3 with bisect and a DLQ; boto3 standard retries; 10 s function timeout (30 s for the aggregator); all functions are stateless (state only in DynamoDB).
Gap: boto3 client connect/read timeouts are defaults (60 s) - longer than the 10 s function timeout; GetOrder has no fallback to DynamoDB if DAX is unreachable (no graceful degradation); no emergency levers (e.g. a flag to disable analytics or reject writes).

monitor-aws-resources.title: How do you monitor workload resources?
monitor-aws-resources.notes:
Evidence: metrics for API Gateway (per method), Lambda, WAF, SQS DLQ, stream IteratorAge aggregated on a dashboard (sums, p90); Logs Insights used for analysis; end-to-end X-Ray traces API Gateway -> Lambda -> DynamoDB.
Gap: NO notifications (no CloudWatch alarms, no SNS topic) and no automated responses; monitoring scope never reviewed.

adapt-to-changes.title: How do you design your workload to adapt to changes in demand?
adapt-to-changes.notes:
Evidence: inherent to the managed serverless services used - Lambda concurrency, DynamoDB on-demand capacity and API Gateway scale automatically with demand and replace impaired capacity without action.
Gap: never load tested - the account's Lambda concurrency quota, the 100 req/s stage limit and the WAF rule were not validated under load.

tracking-change-management.title: How do you implement change?
tracking-change-management.notes:
Evidence: deployment runbook in the README and scripts; unit tests gate every deploy and a smoke test runs after it (CI), plus a 10-check smoke test in scripts/smoke_test.sh; each deploy publishes new immutable code packages through CloudFormation; changes deploy automatically from main.
Gap: no resiliency testing as part of deployment.

backing-up-data.title: How do you back up data?
backing-up-data.notes:
Evidence: point-in-time recovery (continuous, 35 days) on the Orders table in both regions, encrypted with KMS (template.yaml L77-92); automatic, no manual steps.
Gap: OrderStats has no PITR and there is no script to rebuild it from Orders (the stream keeps only 24 h); a restore has never been tested (no periodic recovery test).

fault-isolation.title: How do you use fault isolation to protect your workload?
fault-isolation.notes:
Evidence: all services are multi-AZ managed services; order data is replicated to us-west-2 (global table, RPO < 1 s).
Gap: the API tier exists in one region only; no bulkhead/cell design (one shared stage throttle, no reserved concurrency per function); the optional DAX cluster is a single node with no automated recovery (documented as demo-only).

withstand-component-failures.title: How do you design your workload to withstand component failures?
withstand-component-failures.notes:
Evidence: AZ-level failover and healing are handled by the managed services (Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB); the us-west-2 replica is read/write.
Gap: failures are not detected (no alarms) and nobody is notified; region failover requires deploying the stack in us-west-2 (control-plane dependent, not statically stable); no availability target/SLA defined.

testing-resiliency.title: How do you test reliability?
testing-resiliency.notes:
Evidence: post-incident analysis written for every real problem (README 'Observations and lessons learned', playbook gotchas).
Gap: no failure-investigation playbooks, no load/scalability test, no chaos experiments (e.g. AWS FIS) and no game days.

planning-for-recovery.title: How do you plan for disaster recovery (DR)?
planning-for-recovery.notes:
Evidence: DR strategy for data = DynamoDB global table (us-east-1 + us-west-2) + PITR; the full stack is recreated from code - teardown -> rebuild -> 10/10 smoke checks proven on 2026-10-18/19 (4m38s). DR scenarios documented (README exercise 11 runbook).
Gap: RPO is measured (< 1 s) but no RTO is defined; region failover of the API tier was never exercised; no automated recovery; DR region config is not kept in sync (only the table exists there).

cloud-financial-management.title: How do you implement cloud financial management?
cloud-financial-management.notes:
Evidence: the owner is responsible for cost; cost awareness built into the process - hourly-billed resources behind EnableCaching, decommissioned when idle, CI skips deploy while torn down, cost estimate per scenario (docs/cost-estimate.md).
Gap: NO AWS Budget exists in the account (checked 2026-10-24) and no cost anomaly monitor - cost is not monitored proactively or reported.

not_applicable_choices.cost_cloud_financial_management_partners: Single-person project - no separate finance function.

govern-usage.title: How do you govern usage?
govern-usage.notes:
Evidence: written policy - billable-by-the-hour resources only behind a parameter toggle, demo then disable (playbook section 9); IAM group admins and a narrowly scoped CI deploy role; lifecycle tracked (README status 'Decommissioned', rebuild/teardown scripts).
Gap: no cost goals/targets, single account shared by several projects (no account structure), no cost controls (budget actions).

monitor-usage.title: How do you monitor your cost and usage?
monitor-usage.notes:
Evidence: every resource tagged project=serverless-orders (samconfig tags + resource tags).
Gap: tag not confirmed as an activated cost allocation tag; no Cost and Usage Report, budgets or Cost Explorer views configured; no unit metric (cost per order).

decomissioning-resources.title: How do you decommission resources?
decomissioning-resources.notes:
Evidence: scripts/teardown.sh deletes everything billable and then lists stacks, tables (both regions), clusters, VPCs, queues, functions, APIs, ACLs, pools and log groups to prove nothing is left; the project was decommissioned on 2026-10-19; retention enforced: logs 14 days, DLQ 14 days, dedupe markers TTL 7 days.
Gap: decommissioning is manual (no scheduled/automatic shutdown).

select-service.title: How do you evaluate cost when you select services?
select-service.notes:
Evidence: docs/cost-estimate.md prices every component from the Price List API; per-component analysis (API Gateway detailed metrics $10.50, WAF $6.67, dashboard $3); choices made for cost: arm64, on-demand DynamoDB, direct integration instead of Lambda for reads, gateway endpoint instead of NAT, caching off by default; only open-source software (Powertools, DAX client).
Gap: no analysis of cost at different usage levels over time.

type-size-number-resources.title: How do you meet cost targets when you select resource type, size and number?
type-size-number-resources.notes: Evidence: cost model with two scenarios (caching off ~= $31.70/month, on ~= $90/month at 100k orders); memory sized from Power Tuning data (cost vs speed, balanced); Lambda, DynamoDB on-demand and API Gateway size themselves automatically from demand.

pricing-model.title: How do you use pricing models to reduce cost?
pricing-model.notes: Gap: all components use on-demand list prices; on-demand vs provisioned DynamoDB capacity, Compute Savings Plans and region price differences were not analysed (all small at current volume).

not_applicable_choices.cost_pricing_model_master_analysis: Standalone account, no AWS Organization / management account.

data-transfer.title: How do you plan for data transfer charges?
data-transfer.notes:
Evidence: DynamoDB gateway VPC endpoint (free) instead of a NAT gateway for the DAX VPC; no NAT gateways at all.
Gap: data transfer not modelled in the cost estimate (cross-region replication traffic to us-west-2 is included in replicated writes only).

manage-demand-resources.title: How do you manage demand, and supply resources?
manage-demand-resources.notes: Evidence: traffic profile analysed for the estimate (~0.4 req/s average); throttling at the stage and WAF; stream batching (100 records / 5 s) buffers analytics work; all compute and storage supplied on demand.

evaluate-new-services.title: How do you evaluate new services?
evaluate-new-services.notes:
Evidence: this Well-Architected review and its documented process (well-architected-review/01-how-to-do-a-review.md).
Gap: this is the first review - no regular review cadence yet.

evaluate-cost-effort.title: How do you evaluate the cost of effort?
evaluate-cost-effort.notes: Evidence: build, deploy, rebuild, teardown, smoke tests and cold-start/replication measurements are scripted (scripts/, CI workflow).

securely-operate.title: How do you securely operate your workload?
securely-operate.notes:
Evidence: fully managed serverless services (no servers, OS or patching to manage); security controls are deployed from IaC (default authorizer, WAF, encryption, least-privilege roles).
Gap: one AWS account shared by several projects (no multi-account structure); account-level hardening gaps found (account-level settings were checked read-only on 2026-10-24; the specific findings are kept private and are not published in this repository.); no threat model, control objectives or regular review of new security services.

identities.title: How do you manage identities for people and machines?
identities.notes:
Evidence: no secrets in code or repo; machines use roles (Lambda, API Gateway, CI via GitHub OIDC); IAM group admins; Cognito group admins for analytics.
Gap: Cognito users have no MFA; no periodic credential audit/rotation process. Account-level settings were checked read-only on 2026-10-24; the specific findings are kept private and are not published in this repository.

permissions.title: How do you manage permissions for people and machines?
permissions.notes:
Evidence: each function has a SAM policy template scoped to one table (template.yaml L113-116, L367-379, L629-633, L676-678); API Gateway role = dynamodb:Query on one table (L708-731); CI deploy role can only drive change sets on this stack and pass one role, trust pinned to repo id + main (infra/github-oidc.yaml).
Gap: the CloudFormation execution role has AdministratorAccess (assumable only by CloudFormation); no guardrails (SCPs/permission boundaries), no analysis of public/cross-account access, no emergency access process, no regular permission reduction.

not_applicable_choices.sec_permissions_share_securely: No AWS Organization; no resources shared with other accounts.
not_applicable_choices.sec_permissions_share_securely_third_par: No resources shared with third parties.

detect-investigate-events.title: How do you detect and investigate security events?
detect-investigate-events.notes: Gap: API Gateway access logs and WAF logs are not enabled - application logs exist, but security events are neither captured centrally nor alerted on. Account-level detection services: account-level settings were checked read-only on 2026-10-24; the specific findings are kept private and are not published in this repository.

network-protection.title: How do you protect your network resources?
network-protection.notes:
Evidence: layers = WAF -> API Gateway -> Lambda -> DynamoDB; the optional DAX cluster sits in private subnets with no internet route; security groups allow only TLS 9111 / 443 from the Lambda security group (template.yaml L491-521).
Gap: WAF has only a rate-based rule - no AWS managed rule groups (Core rule set, Known bad inputs, IP reputation), so no inspection-based protection; no automated network protection.

protect-compute.title: How do you protect your compute resources?
protect-compute.notes:
Evidence: AWS-managed Lambda runtime (python3.12), patched by AWS; no servers or interactive access; all changes through CI/CD.
Gap: no vulnerability scanning of code/dependencies (Amazon Inspector for Lambda, Dependabot) and no Lambda code signing.

data-classification.title: How do you classify your data?
data-classification.notes:
Evidence: protection follows sensitivity informally - order data is per-customer (ownership enforced by the token's sub), store-wide analytics are admin-only, user emails live only in Cognito.
Gap: no written classification scheme; order data has no lifecycle (kept forever); no automated classification.

protect-data-rest.title: How do you protect your data at rest?
protect-data-rest.notes:
Evidence: KMS (aws/dynamodb) for the Orders global table in both regions; SSE on OrderStats, SQS-managed SSE on the DLQ, DAX SSE, encrypted API cache entries - all declared in IaC (template.yaml L77-79, L604-605, L615, L576-577, L329); access only through per-table least-privilege roles.
Note: AWS-managed keys - no customer-managed key policy or rotation control.

protect-data-transit.title: How do you protect your data in transit?
protect-data-transit.notes: Evidence: API Gateway only serves HTTPS with AWS-managed certificates; DAX cluster endpoint encryption TLS (template.yaml L578); all AWS API calls are SigV4-signed over TLS; clients authenticate with Cognito JWTs.

incident-response.title: How do you anticipate, respond to, and recover from incidents?
incident-response.notes: Gap: no incident response plan or playbooks (e.g. leaked key, abusive client, data exposure), no forensic preparation, no simulations.

application-security.title: How do you incorporate and validate the security properties of applications throughout the design, development, and deployment lifecycle?
application-security.notes:
Evidence: deployments only through CI/CD; pipeline security designed and documented (OIDC, no stored keys, trust pinned to immutable repo id and main branch, deploy role scoped to change sets); unit tests include security behaviour (ownership, validation, admin-only analytics) and the CI smoke test asserts 401.
Gap: no regular penetration testing (one manual injection test), no code reviews by a second person, no centralised/scanned dependency source.

sus_region.title: How do you select Regions for your workload?
sus_region.notes: Gap: us-east-1/us-west-2 were chosen as account defaults, not by business requirements combined with sustainability (carbon intensity) goals.

sus_user.title: How do you align cloud resources to your demand?
sus_user.notes:
Evidence: everything scales with demand (to zero when idle); unused assets are removed (caching off by default, whole project decommissioned when not in use); throttling and stream batching flatten demand.
Gap: no SLAs to align; placement not chosen by user location.

sus_software.title: How do you take advantage of software and architecture patterns to support your sustainability goals?
sus_software.notes: Evidence: analytics done asynchronously in batches; low-use components switched off (DAX/API cache) or removed; hot paths optimised with measurements (Power Tuning, init breakdown); data access via keys and pre-computed aggregates instead of scans.

not_applicable_choices.sus_sus_software_a5: Backend API only - no client devices or apps in scope.

sus_data.title: How do you take advantage of data management policies and patterns to support your sustainability goals?
sus_data.notes:
Evidence: DynamoDB key design fits the access patterns; lifecycle via TTL (7-day markers) and 14-day log retention; redundant data removed by TTL and teardown; PITR only on Orders - OrderStats is derived data and not backed up.
Gap: no data classification policy; orders have no expiry.

not_applicable_choices.sus_sus_data_a5: No block storage or file systems - DynamoDB only.
not_applicable_choices.sus_sus_data_a7: No shared file systems - DynamoDB only.

sus_hardware.title: How do you select and use cloud hardware and services in your architecture to support your sustainability goals?
sus_hardware.notes: Evidence: no provisioned servers - pay-per-request managed services only; Graviton (arm64) for every function; managed services throughout.

sus_dev.title: How do your organizational processes support your sustainability goals?
sus_dev.notes:
Evidence: CI/CD lets improvements ship quickly; GitHub-hosted ephemeral runners (no idle build servers).
Gap: no sustainability goals defined; runtime/library updates are manual.

not_applicable_choices.sus_sus_dev_a5: Backend API only - no device testing.
